chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Azrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to wear his ring on his right hand.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.يَتَخَتَّمُ: He wore a ring / He used to wear a ring

ai.seo_question: Did Imam Ali wear his ring on his right or left hand?
ai.summary: This brief narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the Sunnah of wearing the ring on the right hand, a practice often associated with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and later adopted by the Imams. In Shia jurisprudence, this detail is significant for distinguishing between recommended acts of adornment and specific ritual practices, while also reflecting the dignified personal etiquette (adab) of the Ahl al-Bayt. It underscores the continuity of prophetic traditions within the Imamate, linking the spiritual authority of Ali (peace be upon him) to the broader Islamic heritage of modesty and distinction.
